decision: One distinct source-diagnosis task warrants bounded product verification; no new route approved or drafted.
task: Identify and correct the source of a missing or wrong contact birthday without creating a duplicate annual event or confusing app-only visibility with cross-device synchronization.

nextAction.action: Read-only native audit of device Birthdays calendar loading, direct Google birthday handling and contact permissions, then decide whether a substantive provider-labelled section in the all-day guide suffices. If the verified workflow needs a standalone guide, choose one birthday-source canonical, not separate missing/duplicate/reminder keyword pages.
specificQuestions: Does Cloud display the Apple system Birthdays source through EventKit and under which calendar selection/read-permission conditions?
Do direct Google calendar downloads include provider birthday events or special birthday-calendar cases, and are updates one-time or recurring?
Does Cloud itself read/edit contact birthday fields, or must a provider/system Contacts editor be used?
Which existing widget and alert limitations apply to these all-day records without promising a birthday-specific widget or reminder?
nextAction.scopeGate: No Cloud Contacts import, automatic contact mirroring, birthday editor, provider setting or refresh deadline established by this discovery. Do not transfer Google app controls or a competitor’s features to Cloud.
nextAction.whyNotDraftNow: Current official Google guidance includes source-edit and removal effects that differ from a simplistic Apple-derived read-only birthday model. The actual Cloud connection path changes the correct next action.

ledgerAndCorpus.readScope: All ten current cluster IDs/statuses inspected, including published deleted-event recovery.
ledgerAndCorpus.priorCandidate: research/competitors/batch26-original-corpus-completion-20261022.json had already identified Contacts birthdays as a possible future task, explicitly without complete body audit. This batch supplies fresh search/provider evidence and direct canonical comparison.
ledgerAndCorpus.notRetried: No original failed URLs or malformed Fantastical path opened. No original-corpus URL reopened merely to raise review counts.

search.query: birthday calendar iPhone contacts missing birthdays BusyCal Fantastical official
search.toolScope: One public web search query; not a fixed-location Google SERP or ChatGPT recommendation test.
search.limits: Selected observed results, not exhaustive result export or rank claims. Third-party proxy Apple URLs were not adopted as official evidence; official Apple host opened separately. Reddit discussions, old PDFs, App Store release-note snippets and unread Fantastical pages were not used as factual body evidence.

primaryReads.scope: Main guide, all FAQ, product section and source list. Initial view ended around FAQ start; followup supplied remaining body. Images, linked guides and app not tested.
primaryReads.finding: Publisher separates contact-card birthday fields, owning contact account, calendar visibility and alerts; it distinguishes optional contact import from ongoing contact synchronization for its own product.
primaryReads.boundary: Publisher’s iCloud delay and Apple instructions require primary corroboration before reuse. Its birthday-specific widgets/countdowns/import/privacy claims are not Cloud capabilities.

primaryReads.finding: Google distinguishes Contacts-linked birthdays from manually created birthday events. Calendar edits can update linked Google Contacts; deleting a birthday has a different contact-data effect. Disabling Sync from Contacts removes synced events and edits. Device Apple Contacts birthdays have iPhone/iPad-specific visibility rather than Google web/Android synchronization.
primaryReads.boundary: These are Google Calendar app controls and behaviour, not Cloud controls. Do not recommend disabling sync as a harmless visibility test or assume all birthday sources propagate identically.

primaryReads.scope: Followup redirected to en-euro; main create/edit/calendar Birthdays body completely visible. Initial long navigation output truncated, not counted as complete navigation read.
primaryReads.finding: Apple documents a special iCloud Birthdays calendar derived from iCloud Contacts, with changes made in Contacts. Web Calendar requires tablet/computer; calendar display is distinct from source data.
primaryReads.boundary: This page does not establish Cloud Contacts access or an iPhone daily refresh guarantee. Exact regional redirect is retained rather than silently collapsing URL variants.

existingCoverageComparison.coverage: Substantive birthday date labels, date span, free/busy, all-day widget exclusion, transfer boundaries and alerts. Does not distinguish generated contact birthday source from an editable manual yearly event.
existingCoverageComparison.possiblePlacement: Source-identification section before event editor advice, conditional on verified Cloud path.

existingCoverageComparison.coverage: Complete edit-scope/exception/permission guide. Birthday is an example of a continuing repeat; no contact-source diagnosis.
Explicit birthday all-day exclusion and same-device/selection checks. No new birthday-widget guide needed; link this existing explanation.
Complete alert/source-app/selection/system delivery diagnosis. No birthday contact-account generation workflow. Keep general notifications here.

allEnglishCoverageCheck.method: Parsed every current article object, reviewed every title/canonical and searched all string fields for birthday/birthdays/contacts/anniversary roots; output relevant hits and read four matching complete guides. This is not a fresh complete read of all 55 bodies. A final new-route approval should retain this distinction.

articles.title: All-day calendar events: dates, availability and missing widget entries
articles.scope: complete object read this batch

topicHits.text: A birthday, public holiday or trip label can belong to a date without requiring an arrival hour. A dentist visit or a conference session needs an actual start and end time. Choose the representation that lets someone understand the commitment without guessing.

For a one-day birthday, check that it appears on the intended date without an unwanted extra day. For a three-day trip, check all three dates. If you change an existing repeating entry, follow the recurrence guide before saving: choosing All-day does not establish whether an edit affects one occurrence or future occurrences.

If you need a day blocked for leave, check the owning provider's availability or out-of-office controls and the saved result. If you only want a birthday label, check that it does not block time unintentionally. This guide does not promise that Cloud Calendars exposes every provider's availability control or prevents scheduling conflicts. Use a supported provider editor when you need an option absent from the app.

Cloud Calendars' upcoming-event widgets and Live Activity follow future timed appointments. They exclude all-day entries. A birthday may therefore be present in the full calendar but absent from the next-event display. Making the widget larger does not change that eligibility rule.

Open the date in the app and check that the calendar is selected. If the entry is present there, distinguish an expected widget omission from lost calendar data. Do not convert a birthday into an artificial timed meeting merely to make a widget show it; decide first whether the event itself should really have an hour.

A label across the top of a day is useful context, but it is not a reminder that has been delivered. If you need to act before a birthday, deadline or trip, inspect the saved alert and the app and system notification settings. The event's visible date alone does not guarantee an audible reminder.
